measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, D, A, D where the asset was B, D, A, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Reads as a 9mm pistol lying on its side in every view: a long slide (sides.png left and right views), a grip angled off it (front-left and back-left views), and a trigger guard loop (below view). No part sticks out or is missing that the brief names. The grip is thick and blocky, but it stays within a pistol's outline.

M2.reason: Measured length is 9.6 against the brief's 10, a 4.4% difference, well inside 15%. The brief gives no other size, so width and height are not held.

M3.reason: The brief names a slide, a grip, a trigger and a guard, and the guard is there: a bare loop in the below view and the front-left view. The trigger, which every Valve gun in the line-up shows, is not distinct inside that loop in any view, so it is charged as missing. The slide, grip and muzzle end are present. A front sight and a magazine base are not named and are not charged.

M4.reason: The brief asks for black and grey polymer and steel. The sides and the first-person view show a near-black grip and frame with grey slide faces, the same split of colours. Nothing is in a colour the brief does not give.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings or panel detail, so none is asked for. The slide lacks the game's serrations seen in the right half of first-person.png, which is not charged.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. In the line-up (lineup.png, A) the asset was picked as the non-Valve model in 2 of 4 readings, below the three-of-four catch line, so it passed as one of the game's in the test. Its flat, plain shading beside the grenade and the .357 is what made it stand out to the judges.

M7.reason: Lying on its side as the brief says: the front and left views show it low and long, and the front-left and back-left views show it flat on the floor. Its front, the muzzle end, is at the small tab in the left view. Upright and lying match the brief.

M8.reason: The SMAK check passes (no check errors). At 216 triangles it is under twice the median of Half-Life's weapons (142, twice is 284) and under the most any of them spends (291). Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating in the sides or the angle views.

W1.reason: In the first-person view the gun sits in the right hand, muzzle up, grip in the black sleeve and hand, in the same place as the game's own gun (first-person.png left and right). Through the attack (attack.png, shoot 0/14 to 14/14) the grip stays in the hand in every frame, and the gun moves with it without leaving.
